title: Review: Standard enthalpies of formation and combustion; Calorimetry; Hess's law cycles; Maxwell–Boltzmann and catalysts
source: Questions copied unchanged from the mission-lesson scripts for OCR A-level (A) Chemistry (status of the source: mission-lesson scripts of Oct-Nov 2026 (reviewed by AI reviewers; not signed off by a person)). Terms and clues: EN05#t3 term and clue written for the game; EN05#t1 term and clue written for the game; EN05#t2 term and clue written for the game; KN03#t1 term and clue written for the game. Questions: EN02#N.13, EN04#N.10, EN05#N.6, KN03#N.12, EN02#N.8, EN04#N.9a, KN03#N.3a, EN02#N.11a, EN02#N.5a. Some questions repeat from the worlds it reviews.

assemble.prompt: Match each term to its definition.

items.label: Enthalpy of combustion
items.clue: ΔH for complete burning, with carbon ending as CO₂(g) and hydrogen as H₂O(l).

items.label: Standard state
items.clue: The pure, normal form of a substance under the reference conditions, e.g. Br₂(l).

items.label: Enthalpy of formation
items.clue: ΔH when exactly 1 mol of a compound is made from its elements; zero for an element.

items.label: Activation energy
items.clue: On a profile, the height from the reactants up to the top of the barrier; always positive.

questions.stem: A student measures the enthalpy change when potassium chloride dissolves in water. The temperature falls. The student uses a thin glass beaker with no lid instead of an insulated cup. How does the student's value of ΔH compare with the accepted value?

options.text: Less positive: energy flows in from the warmer room, so the fall in temperature is too small.
More positive: heat escapes from the solution to the room, so the fall in temperature is too big.
Less positive: the glass gives out cold to the room, so the fall in temperature is too small.
The same: ΔH depends only on the amount of KCl dissolved, not on the container.

questions.stem: Graphite turns into diamond only at enormous pressures, so ΔH for C(s, graphite) → C(s, diamond) can't be measured directly. But both forms burn. (1) C(s, graphite) + O₂(g) → CO₂(g), ΔH = −393.5 kJ mol⁻¹ · (2) C(s, diamond) + O₂(g) → CO₂(g), ΔH = −395.4 kJ mol⁻¹. What is ΔH for graphite → diamond?
questions.explanation: Keep (1); reverse (2), so its ΔH becomes +395.4. Add: CO₂ and O₂ cancel. ΔH = −393.5 + 395.4 = +1.9 kJ mol⁻¹.

questions.stem: Which equation represents the standard enthalpy change of combustion of ethanol?
questions.explanation: 1 mol of ethanol burns completely to CO₂(g) and H₂O(l). Check: 7 O atoms on each side.

questions.stem: A mixture of hydrogen and oxygen can stay unchanged at room temperature for years. In Döbereiner's lamp (1823), a jet of hydrogen in air strikes a piece of platinum and reacts at once, with no flame or spark to start it. Which explanation is correct?

options.text: The platinum heats the gas, so the curve moves to higher energy and more molecules exceed the same Ea.
The platinum gives a route with a lower Ea, so at the same temperature far more molecules have enough energy.
The platinum makes the reaction more exothermic, so the molecules gain the energy they need to react.
The platinum changes the shape of the curve, moving its peak to higher energy without heating.

questions.stem: Why is the line after the highest reading extrapolated back to the time of mixing?

options.text: It removes random errors in the individual temperature readings.
It corrects for the heat absorbed by the cup and thermometer.
It shows the time at which the reaction finished and the temperature stopped rising.
It corrects for heat lost to the air while the reaction is still going.

questions.explanation: Heat escapes all the while the reaction runs. Extrapolating estimates the temperature reached if it had all happened at once, with no loss.

questions.stem: Use the enthalpy changes of reactions 1 and 2 to calculate ΔH for the decomposition of hydrogen peroxide: 2H₂O₂(l) → 2H₂O(l) + O₂(g). Reaction 1: H₂(g) + O₂(g) → H₂O₂(l), ΔH₁ = −187.8 kJ mol⁻¹. Reaction 2: 2H₂(g) + O₂(g) → 2H₂O(l), ΔH₂ = −571.6 kJ mol⁻¹.
questions.explanation: Reverse and double reaction 1: +375.6. Add reaction 2: −571.6. 2H₂ and one O₂ cancel. ΔH = −196.0 kJ mol⁻¹.

questions.stem: Which energy profile correctly shows an endothermic reaction?

options.text: Products higher than reactants; Ea arrow from the reactants up to the peak; ΔH arrow from reactants up to products.
Products higher than reactants; Ea arrow from the products up to the peak.
Products lower than reactants; ΔH arrow pointing down; Ea arrow from reactants up to the peak.
Products higher than reactants; Ea arrow from the reactants up to the products level.

questions.explanation: Endothermic means products are higher in energy. Ea runs from the reactants to the top of the barrier; ΔH from reactants to products.

questions.stem: A spirit burner containing ethanol, C₂H₅OH, is used to heat 150.0 g of water in a copper can. Burning 0.920 g of ethanol raises the temperature of the water from 19.0 °C to 40.5 °C. Use c(water) = 4.18 J g⁻¹ K⁻¹ and Ar values H 1.01, C 12.01, O 16.00. What value of ΔH for the combustion of ethanol do these results give?

50.0 cm³ of 1.00 mol dm⁻³ HCl(aq) is placed in a polystyrene cup and 25.0 cm³ of 1.00 mol dm⁻³ NaOH(aq) is added. The temperature of the mixture rises by 4.50 °C. HCl(aq) + NaOH(aq) → NaCl(aq) + H₂O(l). Assume that the solutions have a density of 1.00 g cm⁻³ and a specific heat capacity of 4.18 J g⁻¹ K⁻¹. What is ΔH for the reaction?
